payload.title: lat4a x kcnh2a reproduce flying-fish fin PROPORTION in zebrafish (Daane et al. 2021)
payload.statement: In zebrafish, combining lat4a (an L-type amino-acid transporter) and kcnh2a (a potassium channel) alleles reproduces the paired-fin proportion characteristic of flying fishes, and ectopic kcnh2a expression alone drives fin overgrowth. The authors state: 'a combination of alleles from both genes is sufficient to reproduce the flying fish fin bauplan in the distantly related zebrafish'. A fin-size/proportion result in the zebrafish model.
payload.context: Danio rerio (zebrafish); forward-genetic screen + CRISPR against lat4a; readout fin length vs standard length. Concerns fin PROPORTION, not flight; no flight assay performed.
assumptions: Full text read from the NOAA repository PDF (47 pp) plus the Europe PMC abstract.

Figure 4 shows the lat4a;kcnh2a double mutant with wild-type-sized medial fins but overgrown paired fins (paraphrased); the exact plotted B/C normalized-length values are in the figure panels / Data S1A, not the body text.
limitations: Functional demonstration is in zebrafish only.
Does NOT establish the mechanism in any exocoetid or halfbeak; no transfer is asserted.
No flight capability is demonstrated by the genetics.

source.locator: Daane et al. 2021 Curr Biol 31(24):5052-5061; NOAA repository full text (47 pp); Abstract; Fig 1B/1C (allometry); Fig 4 legend + panels B/C; Data S1A (exact per-species/per-genotype values); PMC9172250 / DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054
source.access: NOAA repository full-text PDF (pdftotext, 47 pp) + Europe PMC abstract, read 2026-10-31

payload.title: Genome-wide signatures across 35 beloniform species associate K+/amino-acid-transport loci with increased paired-fin size (Daane et al. 2021)
payload.statement: A phylogenomic analysis of over 300,000 loci across 35 species of flying fishes and relatives reports coding and regulatory signatures associated with convergently increased paired-fin size, including 48 of 17,937 genes with convergent evolutionary-rate shifts, among them potassium- and amino-acid-transport genes.
payload.context: Comparative genomics across Beloniformes (Exocoetidae + relatives); targeted multi-species sequencing of conserved non-coding elements. This is an ASSOCIATION (genomic signatures), not a functional test in any flying fish.
assumptions: Convergence called after false-discovery control (paraphrased from the Results).

Full text also reports that the 'flying halfbeaks' Euleptorhamphus and Oxyporhamphus have pectoral allometry intermediate between halfbeaks and flying fishes - living intermediates on the fin-size axis (paraphrased).
limitations: Association only; no functional manipulation in a flying fish.
Links to 'aerial gliding' are the authors' framing; no flight mechanism is demonstrated by the genomics.
Distinct from the zebrafish functional claim [[claim:daane2021-zebrafish-finproportion-phenocopy]]; no transfer between the two is asserted here.

payload.title: Individual flying-fish pectoral-fin aspect ratio ranges 3.0-16.9 (Fish 1990)
payload.statement: Fish (1990) measured the aspect ratio (defined p.394 as wing span squared divided by wing area) of INDIVIDUAL flying-fish pectoral fins as 3.0 to 16.9, maximum in genus Exocoetus. Quote (p.395): 'The aspect ratios (AR) of individual flying fish pectoral fins range from 3.0 to 16.9'. Table III lists Exocoetus to 19.9.
payload.context: 6 exocoetid genera; INDIVIDUAL pectoral fins. Not the whole-wing span^2/area (whose area is pectoral+pelvic+body). Applying this range to a candidate whole-wing b^2/S is a modelling choice, not an identity.
assumptions: Verbatim p.395 quote above; AR definition p.394.
limitations: Text maximum 16.9 vs Table III 19.9 is unreconciled in the source.
An observed envelope of a sample, not a feasibility law.

source.locator: Fish 1990 J Zool 221:391-403; p.394 (WL & AR definitions), p.395 (pectoral AR range), Table II/III

payload.title: Measured flying-fish wing loading spans 11.7-208.9 N/m2 over 199 specimens (Fish 1990)
payload.statement: Fish (1990) measured wing loading (specimen weight divided by wing area, N/m2; wing area defined as the combined areas of the pectoral and pelvic fins continuous through the body) across six exocoetid genera, 199 preserved specimens (mass 0.003-0.53 kg), ranging 11.7 to 208.9 N/m2.
payload.context: 6 genera, 199 preserved specimens; wing area includes the intervening body rectangle between the fins.
assumptions: The stated 11.7 N/m2 lower bound is for a 0.001 kg specimen, outside the 0.003-0.53 kg mass range Fish states (an inconsistency flagged in the source).
limitations: An observed sample envelope, not a demonstrated physical or feasibility limit.
Wing-area denominator differs from the pectoral-only denominator of the pectoral-fin AR claim.

source.locator: Fish 1990 J Zool 221:391-403; p.394 (WL & AR definitions), p.395 (pectoral AR range), Table II/III

payload.title: Darwin's flying-fish passage is an explicit 'imaginary illustration' / conceivability argument (Origin ch. VI)
payload.statement: In On the Origin of Species (ch. VI; 1st ed. 1859 p.182 through 6th ed. 1872 p.140) Darwin calls flying fish 'our imaginary illustration' and argues only subjunctively that flying fish might, if selection had run that way, have been modified into winged animals. It is a conceivability argument against an objection, not a claim that flying fish are becoming flyers.
payload.context: Historical text, public domain; stable across all six British editions (variorum). 'Fluttering fins' is a 19th-c conjecture; the modern known mechanism is passive gliding on held-rigid pectorals plus tail taxiing, not flapping fins.
assumptions: Page locators and cross-edition stability are from the Darwin Online variorum; the wording is stable across all six British editions.
Darwin's description of 'fluttering fins' is a 19th-century conjecture; the modern mechanism is passive gliding, not flapping (paraphrased, not the source's words).
limitations: Darwin never writes 'Exocoetus' in the 1859/1860/1872 editions (independent grep).
Not a prediction of an inevitable evolutionary path and not a claim of actual precursor species.
'Fluttering fins' does not match the modern gliding mechanism.

source.locator: Origin of Species ch. VI 'Difficulties on Theory'; 1859 1st ed p.182, 1869 5th ed p.218, 1872 6th ed p.140
source.access: Darwin Online variorum via r.jina.ai + Project Gutenberg (1228/22764/2009), read 2026-10-31

payload.title: Calibrate the exocoetid aerodynamic envelope-checker against the measured Fish 1990 / Park & Choi values
payload.known_state: The checker (codex-03 + guilds 6612af6; NOT to be rebuilt) encodes C1 wing loading, C2 launch-speed, C5 pectoral-fin AR as arithmetic over declared numbers. Fish 1990 published per-genus r.m.a. fits and measured ranges; Park & Choi measured pectoral AR 9.0-10.7. Saro-Cortes et al. 2022 (robotic model) and Park & Choi 2010 (physical model) show longitudinal stability is configuration-dependent and trades against lift, so C4's static CG-sign pass/fail is narrower than its wording (the Oxyporhamphus refutation survives).
payload.question: Does the checker reproduce the published measured wing-loading and pectoral-fin aspect-ratio of the six exocoetid genera (and Park & Choi's Cypselurus) within a declared numerical tolerance, with a paired mutant that must fail?
payload.novelty_status: Methods calibration; not a novelty claim.
payload.data_access: Fish 1990 r.m.a. coefficients (full-text, in hand); Park & Choi AR (full-text via fetch tool). No new data acquisition needed.
acceptance_criteria: Checker-computed wing loading for each of the 6 genera at their published mean mass matches Fish 1990 Table II within 5%.
The checker's pectoral-fin AR band contains Park & Choi's measured 9.0-10.7.
A mutant that perturbs one published coefficient fails the calibration (must-fail control).
falsifiers: Any genus wing loading deviates more than 5% from Fish 1990 Table II.
The must-fail mutant passes the calibration.
payload.next_action: Run the checker on the six genera's published (mass, wing area) and on Park & Choi's Cypselurus; compare to Table II/III; record a receipt with tolerances; ship the paired mutant. No acceptance is claimed - this is a proposed protocol for root review.
required_capabilities: the exocoetid checker (codex-03 + guilds; do not rebuild)
payload.cost_stop_bounds: CPU only, <=2 threads, <=5 min wall under systemd-run; stop if any source value cannot be located in the full text in hand; no GPU; no paid inference.
downstream_uses: Lets a reader trust the checker's PASS / CANNOT-EVALUATE outputs

source.locator: Fish 1990 J Zool 221:391-403; p.394 (WL & AR definitions), p.395 (pectoral AR range), Table II/III

payload.title: Determine whether the zebrafish lat4a/kcnh2a fin-proportion mechanism is present and active in an exocoetid
payload.known_state: Daane 2021 demonstrates the mechanism functionally in zebrafish [[claim:daane2021-zebrafish-finproportion-phenocopy]] and by genomic association across 35 beloniform species [[claim:daane2021-flyingfish-phylogenomic-association]]. No functional test exists in any exocoetid; no transfer is asserted.
payload.question: Is the lat4a/kcnh2a (bioelectric + amino-acid-transport) fin-proportion mechanism present and functionally active in an exocoetid paired fin, rather than being a zebrafish-only demonstration plus a genomic association?
payload.novelty_status: Open; Daane 2021 explicitly leaves the in-exocoetid functional test undone.
payload.data_access: No exocoetid fin transcriptomics/functional dataset located (bounded search 2026-10-31). One scaffold genome GCA_018398805.1; SRA 53 records.
acceptance_criteria: An exocoetid paired-fin dataset shows lat4a/kcnh2a expression consistent with the zebrafish mechanism, OR a functional perturbation in an appropriate model alters exocoetid-relevant fin proportion as predicted.
falsifiers: Only phylogenomic association is obtainable and no in-exocoetid expression or functional evidence exists; the transfer then remains explicitly unestablished.
payload.next_action: Search public exocoetid RNA-seq / SRA (53 records) for paired-fin lat4a/kcnh2a expression; if none, record searched-not-found and stop. No wet-lab, no flight inference, no bio-transfer asserted. Proposed only; no acceptance claimed.
payload.cost_stop_bounds: CPU only; bounded SRA metadata search <=30 min; stop at first clear negative; no GPU; no paid inference.
downstream_uses: Labels the molecule->fin bridge as established or unestablished
Informs precursor-inspired print labelling (no flight claim)

payload.title: Test whether fin proportion predicted by the genetic model corresponds to the observed exocoetid pectoral allometry
payload.known_state: Daane 2021 measured fin length vs standard length across the clade (Fig 1B) and a zebrafish phenocopy (Fig 4); Fish 1990 measured exocoetid pectoral share (76-92%) and pectoral-fin AR [[claim:fish1990-individual-pectoral-fin-aspect-ratio]].
payload.question: Does the fin proportion predicted by the zebrafish genetic model (lat4a x kcnh2a) correspond, within a declared error, to the observed exocoetid pectoral allometry (Fish 1990; Daane Fig 1B)? A discrepancy is itself a new open question about the missing bridge.
payload.novelty_status: Open; a predicted-vs-observed correspondence cross-check is not published.
payload.data_access: Observed: Fish 1990 (full-text, in hand). Model: Daane 2021 now full-text (NOAA repository PDF); the exact Figure 4 B/C normalized fin-length values are in the figure panels / Data S1A supplement, not in the body text (reduced blocker, not resolved).
acceptance_criteria: The genetic-model fin proportion (Daane Fig 4) and the observed exocoetid pectoral allometry (Fish 1990 / Daane Fig 1B) agree within a declared tolerance.
falsifiers: The two disagree beyond the declared tolerance, in which case record a discrepancy and open a missing-bridge question; do NOT infer transfer in either direction.
payload.next_action: Obtain the Fig 4 B/C plotted values from Data S1A (or digitize the panels); place beside Fish 1990's pectoral allometry; compute the correspondence with a stated tolerance. If Data S1A is not retrievable, record the residual blocker and stop. Proposed only; no acceptance claimed.

payload.cost_stop_bounds: CPU only; stop if Daane source data remain unreachable; no extrapolation beyond measured ranges; no bio-transfer inference.

payload.title: Robotic flying-fish model: a stability-lift trade-off; longitudinal stability only at posterior pelvic positions and negative pitch (Saro-Cortes et al. 2022)
payload.statement: A robotic model of a four-winged flying fish (Reynolds number 30,000) has aerodynamic efficiency maximised with the pelvic fin behind the pectoral and at positive pitch, but is never longitudinally stable at positive pitch and is stable only at the posterior pelvic positions with negative pitch. The authors report 'a clear trade-off between stability and lift generation', with an optimal pelvic configuration that depends on locomotion stage.
payload.context: Physical ROBOTIC model (not a live fish, not a numerical fish simulation); pelvic position H1-H5 and pitch -10 to +5 deg. Lift coefficient for H5 ~0.4 (0.33-0.52); no L/D values reported.
assumptions: Read full-text via WebFetch (fetch tool), 2026-10-31; HOST claude-15 confirmed the article URL is browser-reachable (the 403s were path-specific, not paywall).
limitations: A robotic physical model at Re~30,000, not a live exocoetid; no coefficients transferred to a fish.
No flight capability of any animal is established.

This QUALIFIES constraint C4: static longitudinal stability is configuration-dependent (pelvic position, pitch, deployment) and trades against lift - narrower than a single CG-sign pass/fail. The Oxyporhamphus refutation survives because CG-aft is a body-plan fact, not a deployment state.

source.locator: Saro-Cortes et al. 2022, Integr Comp Biol 62(5):1202; Abstract; Conclusions; 'Pelvic fin parametric study'
source.access: full-text via WebFetch (fetch tool), read 2026-10-31; article URL (path mattered, not paywall)

payload.title: Physical models of Cypselurus hiraii: pelvic fins raise lift and L/D; stability enhanced with both fins; L/D max near 0 deg, lift peaks 30-35 deg; ground effect reduces drag (Park & Choi 2010)
payload.statement: Wind-tunnel measurements on PHYSICAL MODELS of Cypselurus hiraii (not live fish), in three configurations, report that pelvic fins increase lift and lift-to-drag via a jet-like flow between pectoral and pelvic fins; with both fins spread, longitudinal static stability is enhanced; L/D is maximum near 0 deg angle of attack while the lift coefficient peaks at 30-35 deg (where flying fish are observed to leave the water); the glide polar is comparable to hawk, petrel and wood duck; induced drag from wing-tip vortices is a dominant component; and ground effect near the surface reduces drag and raises L/D.
payload.context: Physical models of C. hiraii in a wind tunnel. Abstract/relayed grade; numeric L/D values live only in figures and were not extracted.
assumptions: Abstract-level facts (free) relayed via HOST claude-15. Provenance discipline: a 403 is a fact about the client, not the document; 'no OA copy indexed by OpenAlex/Europe PMC' is NOT evidence none exists (no author-page or institutional-repository search was done).
limitations: No coefficients extracted; no calibrated-fish claim supported.
